Good resistance band exercises for a noob?

Basically you kinda want to strive for the same movements that people do with weights. Think in terms of the large muscle groups - back, chest, arms, legs, abdominals. The big movements are all the same: squats, bench press, shoulder press, rows. I think with resistance bands and perhaps a small selection of light dumbbells you can really do quite a lot.

I recently had an injury that prevented me having good grip strength and so I bought some resistance bands to help me through the rough patch. I found myself picking quite a few exercises out of the first routine outlined here. It looks very solid and well-rounded. Though I wonder if anyone would have suggestions for working hamstrings with RBs?
Thank you so much! That link has lots of great exercises on it! Were there any exercises specifically that helped your grip strength?

My grip weaknesses was more of a function of my tennis elbow - which is really just an inflammation/irritation of the common extensor tendon - so really I just kinda had to take it easy and let it heal, tho not avoid it altogether. That said I used the red Thera-band Flexbar quite a bit as therapy. Regular heavy dumbbells and barbells were just too much weight and caused me to flex and extend my wrist, which was a movement I was trying to avoid heavy weight on. Which is why I picked up the resistance bands - as they allowed me to keep my wrist perfectly stable. Between those and the flexbar, I really managed to get over the injury in the span of a couple months.

I think most non-injured people just squeeze a ball or those little spring-grips to build up grip-strength.
